Subject: Post-call: MirrorWorks inference topology & next steps (latency SLOs)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum going.

High-level goals you shared
- Serve conversational product recommendations to end-users (query+context) with p95 latency target <= 150ms for short requests (~128 tokens).
- Batch background embed jobs for nightly indexing (throughput requirement ~50k embeddings/hour).
- Strong data residency and audit logging needs (EU-sensitive but primary users are in US today).

Primary pain points
- Current hosted endpoint experiences 300–400ms p95; costs blow up with naive horizontal scaling.
- Cache misses on personalized context are common; KV cache sizing unknown.
- Procurement visibility: need an SLA and evidence for audit team before vendor approval.

Technical notes from call
- Model family: you prefer a 7B–13B open model for latency/cost balance; may evaluate a 70B for high-compute batch experiments.
- Expected concurrency: 800 active users at peak, avg 3 requests/sec per user (bursting patterns).
- Preferred deployment: start on Redwood Hosted API to iterate quickly, then move to Dedicated pool once baseline throughput validated. Private (VPC) considered if audit requires network isolation.

Proposed next steps (action owners)
1) Send SLO/ops doc + topology sketch (attached) — David (today).
2) MirrorWorks to share KV cache hit-rate sample + representative prompt set (Samira) — by EOD Tue.
3) Redwood to produce initial capacity estimate + cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated (Marissa) — by Thu EOD.
4) Procurement checklist & contract questions (Neha) — set up separate thread once MirrorWorks confirms procurement contacts.

Attachments included: mirrorworks_slo_requirements.pdf (SLO sheet), inference_topology_sketch.png (draft topology), MW-MutualActionPlan-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan template).

If anything above looks off, flag it here and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll kick off the capacity estimate and loop in engineering for a short proof-of-concept target (we can scope a 2-week POC to validate 128-token p95).

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical specifics we discussed internally that will shape the capacity estimate: 

- Latency baselines: for a 7B model with optimized kernels on A100/A10 equivalents, we expect p95 (128 tokens) in the 90–140ms band under continuous batching if KV cache hit-rate is >65%. If cache hits drop to 30–40% we should expect p95 to move toward 180–250ms without autoscale.
- Recommended topology for POC: 1) Redwood Hosted endpoint with a dedicated inference pool sized for 200 concurrent streams and dynamic burst to 400 for short windows; 2) enable prefix KV caching + a small LRU local cache on the serving nodes; 3) set batching window to 20ms with adaptive sizing.
- Throughput (embeddings): we’ll provision a separate batch worker cluster for the nightly embed workload — estimate: 6x GPU workers running 8-hour windows to hit ~50k embeds/hour depending on model quantization.

Request for MirrorWorks (to refine estimate):
- Provide a 24–72 hour trace of peak-minute QPS (sample) and token distribution across requests.
- Clarify whether EU data requires separate physical tenancy (if yes, we’ll sketch a Dedicated-in-region topology).

I’ll assemble the capacity/cost delta spreadsheet and share by Thu EOD. If procurement needs the SOC2 artifact immediately, Neha can send the standard pack.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
